q: 301. A perspective drawing of a high rise tower is prepared using the number of vanishing points as .............
explain: For tall structures like a high-rise tower, three-point perspective is used, adding a third vanishing point (above or below) to correctly depict the vertical convergence of lines when viewed from a strongly elevated or low angle.

q: 302. Working drawings are prepared at the stage of .............
explain: Working drawings, containing full dimensions and construction details, are produced during the detail design stage, after the concept has been finalized and before construction execution.

q: 303. A circle in isometric projection appears as .............
explain: Because every face in isometric projection is inclined to the line of sight, a circle drawn on that face is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 304. The distortion in oblique projections can be decreased by .............
options: placing the projection in correct scale
reducing the length of the receding lines
placing the projection obliquely to the plane of projection
enlarging the dimensions parallel to the plane of projection
explain: Reducing the length of the receding lines (as done in cabinet projection, using half scale) decreases the visual distortion/exaggeration that appears in oblique projections compared to full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 305. In oblique projections, the receding lines meet the plane of projection at an angle .............
explain: By definition, oblique projection is characterized by projectors that strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., at an angle less than 90°.

q: 306. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of .............
explain: A concept drawing represents the initial design idea and is prepared before construction begins, to communicate and finalize the overall design intent.

q: 307. The working edge of T-square is used to .............
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square's working (blade) edge is used both to directly draw horizontal parallel lines and to serve as a guiding base against which a set square is placed to draw vertical/inclined lines.

q: 308. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size in mm is .............
explain: To accommodate an A0 sheet (841×1189 mm) with margins for pinning and T-square movement, a larger drawing board of approximately 1500×1000×25 mm is required.

q: 309. Topographic map is used to represent the .............
explain: A topographic map represents both natural details (terrain, rivers, vegetation) and artificial/man-made details (roads, buildings), making 'all of the above' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 310. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of a product including civil construction are known as .............
explain: Working drawings are, by definition, the complete technical drawing set used during the actual manufacturing/construction phase of a product or building.

q: 311. Measurements from scale to the drawings are transferred with the aid of .............
explain: A divider is used to accurately transfer measured lengths directly from a scale onto the drawing sheet without marking or damaging the scale.

q: 312. When a right circular cone is cut by a plane passing through its apex, the curve obtained is .............
explain: A section plane passing through the apex of a cone intersects it along straight generator lines meeting at the apex, producing a triangular section rather than a curved conic section.

q: 313. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle greater than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis exceeds the semi-apex angle of the cone (and it does not pass through the apex), the section obtained is a closed curve — an ellipse.

q: 314. Two point perspective is also known as .............
explain: Two-point perspective, where the object is viewed at an angle so its edges converge to two vanishing points, is also referred to as angular perspective.

q: 315. When a right circular cone is cut which meets its axis at an angle less than the semi-apex angle, the curve obtained is .............
explain: When the cutting plane's angle with the axis is less than the cone's semi-apex angle, the plane intersects both nappes of the cone, producing an open hyperbolic section.

q: 316. The angle between the asymptotes of a rectangular hyperbola is .............
explain: By definition, a rectangular (equilateral) hyperbola has its two asymptotes perpendicular to each other, meeting at 90°.

q: 317. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45° with .............
explain: Standard hatching convention draws section lines at 45° to the main outline or principal axis of the sectioned component, rather than to a fixed horizontal/vertical reference.

q: 318. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing straight line is .............
explain: Effective freehand straight-line sketching typically combines fixing the two end points, judging the overall length, and marking the midpoint as guides, so 'all of the above' applies.

q: 319. One plane projection is .............
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are examples of single (one) plane projection methods, where the entire 3D object is represented on one projection plane, unlike multiview (orthographic) projection which uses multiple planes.

q: 320. Minimum area of ............. square meter should be provided per bed in hospital.
explain: Hospital building design norms in this reference specify a minimum area of 45 m² per bed, accounting for the bed itself plus circulation, medical equipment, and support space.

q: 321. Floor height shall not be less than ............. for Terai region.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 2 m is marked correct for the Terai (plains) region in this reference; this contrasts with the higher 2.5 m minimum specified for hilly regions (Q257) due to differing climatic considerations.

q: 322. Angles in multiples of 15° are constructed by the combined use of .............
explain: By combining a T-square (horizontal reference) with a 45° and 30°-60° set square in various positions, angles in multiples of 15° can be constructed without needing a protractor.

q: 323. To draw or measure angles, we use .............
explain: A protractor is the dedicated instrument specifically designed for accurately drawing and measuring angles on a drawing.

q: 324. Name the curve which has zero eccentricity .............
explain: A circle is the special case of a conic section with eccentricity exactly equal to zero, distinguishing it from an ellipse (0<e<1), parabola (e=1), and hyperbola (e>1).

q: 325. Which of the following curves obeys the Boyle's law?
explain: Boyle's Law (pressure × volume = constant, at constant temperature) describes an inverse relationship (PV=k), which graphically corresponds to a rectangular hyperbola.

q: 326. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'painter' is marked correct here; perspective projection, giving a realistic natural-eye view, is fundamentally used by painters/artists to depict depth and realism in artwork.

q: 327. The representation of any matter by some sign or marks on the drawing is known as .............
explain: Standardized signs, symbols, or marks used to represent specific materials, features, or information on a drawing are collectively called conventions.

q: 328. Picture plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection, the picture plane is the imaginary vertical plane onto which the perspective view of the object is projected, positioned between the observer and the object.

q: 329. Maximum ground coverage ratio for university building is .............
explain: Per this reference's building bye-law norms, university buildings are permitted a maximum ground coverage ratio of 20%.

q: 330. Pictorial views drawn on isometric scale are called .............
explain: When a pictorial view is constructed strictly using the reduced isometric scale (foreshortened lengths, ~0.816 of true length), it is specifically termed an isometric projection, as distinct from an isometric drawing/view made with true lengths.

q: 331. The exact value of R.F. of an Isometric scale is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 9/11 is marked as the exact R.F. value here — an approximate fractional equivalent close to the mathematically derived isometric ratio (√(2/3) ≈ 0.8165).

q: 332. As built drawing is normally constructed .............
explain: As-built drawings are, by definition, prepared after construction is completed, documenting the actual final condition of the built structure.

q: 333. A pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base removing the apex, the remaining part is known as .............
explain: When the apex portion of a pyramid (or cone) is removed by a plane parallel to its base, the remaining solid portion is specifically called a frustum.

q: 334. Scale of chord is used to measure .............
explain: A scale of chords is a specialized scale specifically constructed to measure and construct angles using chord lengths corresponding to given angular values.

q: 335. The nature of lateral surface of cylinder is .............
explain: A cylinder's curved lateral surface bends in only one direction (around its circular cross-section) while remaining straight along its length/axis, making it a singly curved surface, unlike a sphere.

q: 336. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw .............
explain: A parallel ruling straight-edge, sliding vertically on guide wires while remaining horizontal, is designed primarily to draw horizontal parallel lines efficiently.

q: 337. French curve are used to draw .............
explain: A French curve is a template specifically shaped to guide the drawing of smooth irregular curves that are not simple circular arcs.

q: 338. Minimum area of opening for natural ventilation in patient room of hospital and class room is ............. of room area.
explain: Building ventilation norms in this reference specify that the minimum openable area for natural ventilation in hospital patient rooms and classrooms should be at least 1/6 of the room's floor area.
